turns.content: Let n!! denote n(n-2)(n-4)... down to 2 for even n and down to 1 for odd n. Begin with even n: determine exactly which even positive integers satisfy n!! divides 2012!!.
Write 2012!! as 2^1006 times 1006!. Use that factorization to examine the first odd double factorials near the divisibility boundary, including 1007!! and 1009!!.
At the odd boundary, discard the residual factorial and use only the power-of-two factor as an exact divisibility test for 1007!! and 1009!!.
Count the admissible even values of n, making the endpoint and its inclusion explicit.
Check the odd boundary by comparing the prime multiplicities contributed by 1007=19*53 with those available in 1006!, and contrast this with the missing prime 1009.
Use the established boundary to list and count all admissible odd positive integers n.
Combine the even and odd counts to obtain the requested number of positive integers n.
